fundamentals.about: SMT is a Surat-based Class III medical device maker focused on vascular intervention (drug-eluting stents, PTCA balloons) and structural heart products (TAVI valves, occluders). It has two plants in India and one in Thailand, and sold in 77 countries in FY26. It claims nearly 25% share of India's DES volume. Europe is its largest market at 38.66% of FY26 revenue.

objects.purpose: Offer for Sale by Selling Shareholders (company receives no proceeds); listing benefits

promoters.background: Company was founded in 2001 by Dhirajlal Kotadia; Bhargav Kotadia is Managing Director and CEO. Samara Capital (29.61%), NHPEA Sparkle (15.24%) and Kotak Pre-IPO Fund (5.98%) are other large shareholders and sellers in the OFS.

concentration.note: Top 10 distributors were 15.71% of FY26 revenue (26.34% in FY24); top distributor 3.01%; no single customer above 10%. Top 10 countries were 78.76% of FY26 revenue.

fundamentals.litigation_note: Against the Company: 2 criminal, 98 tax and 5 regulatory proceedings with quantifiable amount Rs 131.97 crore; against Directors Rs 24.85 crore (4 criminal, 4 tax); against Promoters Rs 6.10 crore (4 tax); against subsidiaries Rs 7.00 crore. No material civil litigation.
strengths: Nearly 25% share of India's drug-eluting stent volume in FY26 and top-five DES player in Germany, Spain, Poland and Brazil, per the F&S industry report.
Diversified revenue: India 26%, Europe 39% and rest of world 35% in FY26, sold in 77 countries.
Broad Class III portfolio across stents, balloons, TAVI valves and occluders, backed by 75 clinical studies including the Lancet-published TALENT trial.
Strong R&D with 119 patents granted, 78 pending and R&D spend of about 8.6% of FY26 revenue.
Integrated manufacturing in India and Thailand, with large spare capacity (stent utilisation 78% in FY26).
Improving profitability: PAT swung from a Rs 7 crore loss in FY24 to Rs 69 crore profit in FY26; EBITDA margin up to 14.1%.
Falling distributor concentration: top 10 distributors dropped from 26% of revenue in FY24 to 16% in FY26.
Proven acquisition playbook (Imex Spain, Zarek Brazil, Vascular Concepts, Vascular Innovations) and institutional investor backing.

risks.title: High receivables and rising bad debts
risks.detail: Trade receivables were Rs 306.56 crore at June 2026 (76 days of sales); bad debts jumped to Rs 18.56 crore in FY26 from Rs 2.95 crore in FY25. Long credit is extended to distributors.

risks.title: Heavy borrowings and covenant breaches
risks.detail: Borrowings were Rs 320.63 crore at June 2026 (Rs 269.53 crore at March 2026), mostly short-term. The company has breached financial covenants in the past, and a subsidiary breached a term loan covenant in FY26 (waived by lender).

risks.title: Extensive regulatory and certification dependence
risks.detail: Products are Class III devices needing CE and Indian approvals. Many CE certificates under the old MDD expire December 31, 2027 and must move to the stricter EU MDR; only Supraflex Cruz has MDR certification so far.

risks.title: Pure offer for sale, no money to the company
risks.detail: The whole offer is 13,822,116 shares sold by existing investors (13.60% of pre-offer capital); the company receives nothing, so no funds go to debt reduction or growth.

risks.title: Weak debt service coverage
risks.detail: Debt service coverage ratio was only 0.65 in FY26, 0.47 in FY25 and 0.12 in the June 2026 quarter, while interest coverage was 4.29 in FY26.

risks.title: Pending litigation and tax disputes
risks.detail: 98 tax proceedings and 2 criminal cases against the company, with quantifiable amount of Rs 131.97 crore; Directors face Rs 24.85 crore and Promoters Rs 6.10 crore.

risks.title: International operations risk
risks.detail: About 74% of FY26 revenue is outside India (Europe 38.66%, rest of world 35.21%), exposing results to currency, tariff, regulatory and tender risks across 77 countries.

risks.title: Untraceable historical corporate records
risks.detail: Several RoC filings and challans for share allotments since 2001 (items up to 13.68% of pre-offer capital) could not be located, which could invite regulatory action.

risks.title: Litigation and contingent liabilities

fundamentals.about: Coreintegra is a Mumbai-based HR solutions provider offering staffing, vendor management, payroll, labour-law compliance and in-house HR-tech/reg-tech platforms (Ctrl-F, CoreX, Core Pay, Core PFT). It served 385 customers in FY26 across 30+ industries via 7 branch offices, with about 88% of revenue from Maharashtra. The model is asset-light with very thin margins (PAT margin under 1%).

promoters.background: Promoters hold 49,46,874 shares (64.51%); with promoter group (incl. Eureka Outsourcing Solutions) total 93.04% pre-issue. MD Mahesh Krishnamoorthy has about two decades of finance experience.

concentration.note: Top 5 customers were 89.31% of FY26 revenue (88.04% FY25, 90.16% FY24); Customer 1 alone was 53.01% and Customer 2 33.57% in FY26. Maharashtra gives 87.97% of revenue.

fundamentals.litigation_note: RHP notes outstanding legal proceedings involving the company, group company, promoters, directors and KMP; amounts not quantified in the provided index. Contingent liability of Rs 22.61 lakh (performance guarantee for a related enterprise).
strengths: In-house technology platforms (Ctrl-F, CoreX, Core Pay, Core PFT) across the HR and compliance value chain.
Revenue grew from Rs 366 crore in FY24 to Rs 515 crore in FY26, about 18.6% CAGR.
Debt-free: no borrowings in any of the last three years.
High client retention of 90.46% in FY26 and top 10 customers associated for over 3 years.
Presence across 23 states and 4 union territories, serving 1,500+ client locations.
Reported ROCE of 20.19% and ROE of 17.94% in FY26.
ISO 27001:2022 and ISO 9001:2015 certified with 4 registered software copyrights.
Asset-light model with low capital expenditure needs.

risks.title: Extreme customer concentration
risks.detail: Top 5 customers gave 89.31% of FY26 revenue; Customer 1 alone 53.01% and Customer 2 33.57%. Losing one would badly hit revenue.

risks.title: Razor-thin margins
risks.detail: EBITDA margin only 1.17% and PAT margin 0.87% in FY26, so small cost increases can erase profit.

risks.title: Negative operating cash flow and heavy receivables
risks.detail: Operating cash flow was negative Rs 3.05 crore in FY26 (taxes paid Rs 8.09 crore). Receivables are 40.02% of total assets.

risks.title: Revenue concentrated in one state and sector
risks.detail: Maharashtra gave 87.97% of FY26 revenue; IT/ITES and Infra clients make up about 90.9%.

risks.title: Short client contracts without volume guarantee
risks.detail: Contracts are typically 1 year (max 3) and can be terminated on notice, so revenue visibility is limited.

risks.title: Outstanding litigation and past compliance lapses
risks.detail: Legal proceedings pending against company, promoters and directors; past delays in EPF, labour welfare and professional tax payments and RoC filings.

risks.title: Related party dealings
risks.detail: Transactions with director-linked firms including inter-corporate deposits and a Rs 22.61 lakh performance guarantee for a related enterprise.

risks.title: Issue proceeds unappraised and valuation not yet set
risks.detail: Only Rs 18.01 crore of identified uses with no independent appraisal; price band blank and promoters keep control with 64.51% pre-issue.
